supporting_evidence.summary: significant deviations in scope [all services]: frontend_error z=36054091.54; frontend-external_error z=36054091.54; checkoutservice_latency-50 z=117.63 (1761.2%); checkoutservice_latency-90 z=94.85 (1943.2%)
traces for checkoutservice: SIGNIFICANT change; own spans self-time p50 3.98->126.32ms (31.72x), errors 0.0->0.0025; inbound calls self-time p50 2.83->3.43ms (1.21x), errors 0.0->0.1014

significant deviations in scope [service=checkoutservice]: checkoutservice_latency-50 z=117.63 (1761.2%); checkoutservice_latency-90 z=94.85 (1943.2%); checkoutservice_socket z=6.69 (33.4%); checkoutservice_mem z=6.26 (31.3%)

alternatives_rejected.why: CPU is not among checkoutservice's significant deviations. Only latency (z=117.63), socket (z=6.69) and mem (z=6.26) appear (E3), so this is latency without CPU saturation.
checkoutservice's own self-time p50 rose 3.98->126.32ms (31.72x) (E2). That means the time is spent inside checkoutservice, not waiting on its callees.
The frontend error spike (E1) matches inbound errors to checkoutservice rising 0.0->0.1014 (E2). This fits frontend being a caller hit by checkoutservice slowness, not the origin.
The socket (33.4%) and mem (31.3%) deviations are small next to latency-50 (1761.2%) and latency-90 (1943.2%) (E3), so they are more likely side effects of slow requests piling up.

proposed_fix.description: Inspect the checkoutservice pods for injected network latency (for example a tc netem qdisc) or a recent config or deploy change that adds delay, and remove or roll it back. Then confirm checkoutservice p50 and p90 latency and the frontend error rate return to baseline. A pod restart of checkoutservice is a fallback if the cause cannot be found quickly.
